title: Legible Cities engine protocol, version 1
description: JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdin/stdout with Content-Length framing. `methods` maps each request to the schema of its params and result; `notifications` maps each notification to the schema of its params. Long requests (graph.build, map.build, export.encode, feeds.service) stay open until done and send job/progress and job/log carrying the request's id meanwhile; $/cancelRequest ends the process they are waiting on (a LOOM tool, or ffmpeg) and they answer with the cancelled error (-32800). feeds.service starts no process: a cancel is answered with the same error once its read finishes. The export methods are the two halves of an export a client cannot do itself: export.plan describes one and is pure, export.encode turns the frames the client captured into the file; there is no export.capture, because the desktop app captures for itself. Errors a person can act on are code -32000 with `data` of the ErrorData shape; bad parameters are -32602 with the same shape and kind `params`.

RequestId.description: A JSON-RPC request id, as the client chose it.

NoParams.description: The method takes no parameters: omit `params`, or send an empty object.

FeedKey.description: The key of a registered feed: lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, as in the engine's registry and its file names.

Token.description: A folder name under the engine's home, never a path: the desktop app passes its project id.

FeedsServiceParams.description: Ask when a feed runs and which day to draw: its service window and the busiest weekday scanning from an anchor. A long request, like graph.build: it downloads the feed when it is not cached and reads its calendar and trips, and sends no progress.

anchor.description: The day to scan from; the engine's today when omitted, and echoed either way so a caller can store it. An anchor outside the window scans from the window's middle.

lines.description: The lines the map draws, as graph.build names them in stages.octi.lines. Trips are counted on those lines, as the map build counts them, so the day is the map's; every trip in the feed counts when omitted.

start.description: The first day the feed's calendar covers.

busiest_weekday.description: The weekday in the window with the most trips, scanning from the anchor: the same feed and anchor give the same day on every machine.

anchor.description: The anchor the choice was made from.

ServiceDate.description: A calendar day, YYYY-MM-DD. map.build never picks one, because its choice would depend on the day the request was made; feeds.service picks one from an anchor the caller gives.

EngineInfo.description: The handshake. A client refuses to continue unless `protocol` is the version it was built for and `engine` is the tag it pinned.

engine.description: The engine's version, as in its package metadata.

commit.description: The LOOM commit the binaries were built from; null when the backend cannot say.

ffmpeg.description: The ffmpeg the engine would run (SCHEMATIC_FFMPEG, else the first on PATH), or null.

home.description: SCHEMATIC_HOME as resolved: where feeds, graphs and output live.

LayoutId.description: A stored layout's id: the sha256, as 64 hex digits, of everything that went into it. The same feed, options and LOOM name the same id before anything runs; the desktop app stores it with a project.

HexColor.description: A colour a client chooses, written #rrggbb. The feed's own route_color arrives without the hash and is the feed's, not the client's.

LayoutMeta.description: What a stored layout was made from, as written beside it in .meta.json. The inputs are what its id hashes; engine, made and migrated are not.

feed_sha256.description: The sha256 of the feed zip as downloaded.

loom.description: The LOOM commit the host passed as SCHEMATIC_LOOM_COMMIT; null when it was not told.

stages.description: The graph-to-graph stages and their arguments, in order.

engine.description: The engine version that made it.

made.description: When, as an ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC.

migrated.description: True for a set from before layouts had names, moved under its id once; its inputs are the feed and options as they were at migration.

GraphBuildParams.description: Lay a registered feed out: gtfs2graph, topo, loom and octi, stored under the home as one layout named by the hash of its inputs (the feed's bytes, the mode, the agency, the label options, the LOOM build). The same inputs name the same layout; a layout already stored is answered without running anything. Mode, agency and the label options default to the registry entry.

mode.description: What gtfs2graph keeps of the feed (LOOM's -m): names such as tram, subway, rail, bus, ferry or all, or route_type numbers, comma-joined for several; the registry entry's when omitted.

agency.description: Keep only this agency_id; the registry entry's when omitted; empty for every operator, whatever the entry says.

label_pattern.description: A regular expression applied to route_long_name when route_short_name is blank; group 1 is the line's label.

label_strip.description: A regular expression removed from every label.

force.description: Lay the feed out again under the same id. The stored layout stays until the new set is whole, then is replaced; a new layout may place stations differently.

octilinear.description: The share of drawn length on a 45-degree multiple; only the octi stage carries it.

paths.description: Where each stage's GeoJSON is stored, as absolute paths under the home: graphs/<key>/<layout>/.

MapBuildParams.description: Draw the map and the animation page for a registered feed on one service day, from a stored layout. Never lays the feed out: a layout that is not stored is refused, with a hint to lay it out first.

out.description: The folder under the home's out/ to write into. Omitted, the files go into out/ itself.

width.description: The SVG's width in CSS pixels.

colors.description: A colour per line label, over the feed's own route_color. A label the layout does not carry is ignored, so a client can keep colours for lines a narrower mode dropped.

default_color.description: The colour of a line the feed leaves uncoloured, on the map and in the page's chips, dots and chart alike; #888888 when omitted.

line_order.description: Line labels in the order they stack on shared track, the later over the earlier. A line the list leaves out follows the ones it names, and a label the layout does not carry is ignored, so a partial or stale order never drops a line.

unmatched.description: The first few stop ids that matched no node.

summary.description: Result.summary(), the lines the CLI prints.

caveats.description: What the build had to fudge, as sentences a person can read: the atlas's caveats, from the same numbers.

issues.description: How much of the network the build had to fudge, as one weighted proportion; 0 is clean. What the atlas is ordered by.

JobProgress.description: Sent while a long request runs, once per step as it finishes.

JobLog.description: A line a tool wrote to stderr while a long request ran, as it arrived.

PresetName.description: A preset's name; export.presets describes each. Held equal to the engine's table by a test.

StoryboardName.description: A storyboard's name; export.storyboards describes each. Held equal to the engine's table by a test.

View.description: A view the page can show.

Clock.description: A time of day, HH:MM or HH:MM:SS; past midnight stays past midnight (25:44 is 1:44 the next morning).

PageUrl.description: The page's own address, with its scheme. The desktop app serves a project's page on its own origin and passes that; the engine's default is the site's file.

AbsolutePath.description: A path the client owns, absolute, never inside the engine's own repository.

Preset.description: One destination, with the dimensions and limits that destination has.

storyboard.description: Video only: the storyboard the preset plays unless told otherwise.

max_bytes.description: The platform's upload limit, where it has one.

safe_zones.description: Whether the platform draws its own interface over the image.

StoryboardBeat.description: A stretch of video with one set of state, as the storyboard is written. A field left null carries over from the beat before.

views.description: The views it visits, in order, as a sentence fragment; empty for one view.

geographic.description: Whether any beat needs the feed's geographic geometry.

ExportOptions.description: The dressing of an export; every field optional and defaulted as bin/export defaults it.

title.description: The city and network over the map.

at.description: The clock to start at; a still is taken here.

lines.description: Line labels to keep; the rest are hidden.

quality.description: draft: 1x and fast; standard: 2x, resampled to the preset's size; high: 2x, kept.

tag.description: A filename suffix, so two dressings of one preset can share a folder.

safe.description: Draw the platform's safe zones; never for a deliverable.

ExportPlanParams.description: Describe an export: what to capture and how to encode it. Pure and instant; nothing is written. A vector preset is refused (it is resolved from the built map, not captured).

date.description: The service day the title names, when the caller knows it (the app's project does).

BeatPayload.description: A beat as the recorder takes it: times in seconds of the service day, the span resolved.

CaptureJob.description: One export, described: the capture half is the job the engine's own recorder takes (url, width, height in CSS pixels, scale, fps, format, settle, beats, at); the rest is what export.encode needs afterwards. Handed back to export.encode unchanged.

settle.description: Milliseconds to wait, with the clock stopped, for the page's first geometry pass and its fonts.

keep.description: Deliver the captured pixels as they are rather than resampling to the preset's size.

at.description: The clock, in seconds, a still is taken at; a video's beats seek for themselves.

notes.description: What a person should hear before the capture, such as a sweep too fast to read.

filename.description: stem plus the format's extension; the plan's convenience.

Provenance.description: What the caller knows about the map that the atlas's data would not; it goes into the sidecar over the atlas's, field by field.

ExportEncodeParams.description: The frames the client captured (a directory of 000000.png onwards), or its still, to the deliverable at dest with its sidecar beside it. The source is read and never touched; a cancel, a failure or a file over the platform's limit leaves nothing at dest.

source.description: The frames directory for a video plan, the captured still for a still plan.

dest.description: The file to write; its folder is created.

sidecar.description: The sidecar as written beside the file: what it is, the network's caveats, alt text.

FeedRecord.description: A registry entry, preset or added by a person: what the engine knows about a feed before it reads it. `cached` says whether its zip is on disk.

url.description: Where the zip came from; empty for a feed added from a file.

source.description: Which half of the registry: a preset is curated in the engine and cannot be removed; a user feed was added through feeds.add.

FeedsAddParams.description: Add a feed a person chose, from a URL or a zip the client owns, and keep it across restarts. A long request: the download reports its bytes as job/progress (stage download), then the check reports once (stage check). The zip must carry stops, routes, trips, stop_times and a calendar in one of its two forms; a refusal names the missing table and leaves nothing behind. A cancel is honoured until the moment the feed is kept, and answers with the cancelled error (-32800): the feed is then in neither the registry nor the cache, so a client told an add was cancelled need not go looking for one. The name defaults to the feed's first agency, the key to a slug of the name made unique.

source.description: A URL with its scheme, or an absolute path to a zip the client owns.

mode.description: What gtfs2graph keeps of the feed (LOOM's -m); all when omitted. feeds.inspect suggests one.

agency.description: Keep only this agency_id; every operator when omitted.

FeedsRemoveParams.description: Forget a feed a person added, with its zips and its stored layouts. A preset is refused with kind feed.

FeedsInspectParams.description: What is in a feed, as data, before anything is laid out: read from the raw zip, never the agency-filtered copy, so the answer is what a choice of mode and agency is made from. A long request when the feed is not cached; a few seconds for a large one. Never reads stop_times.

anchor.description: The day the service choice scans from, as feeds.service takes it; the engine's today when omitted, and echoed.

label.description: The label the map would draw: route_short_name, or the long name through the feed's label pattern, then the strip.

route_type.description: GTFS route_type as published; -1 when missing.

color.description: route_color as the spec asks for it: six hex digits, upper case, without the hash. Null when the feed leaves it out or writes something that is not a colour, which a client must not paint with.

text_color.description: route_text_color on the same terms as color.

trips.description: Rows in trips.txt; a headway-based trip is a template that expands into runs.

name.description: The GTFS name: tram, subway, rail, bus, ferry, cable tram, aerial lift, funicular, trolleybus, monorail; an extended code says which it folds onto.

mode.description: The LOOM mode (gtfs2graph -m) that keeps this type, so a client can show which types a chosen mode draws; null for a type LOOM has no name for. The mode all keeps every type.

modes.description: Every -m name that keeps this type, the canonical one first (subway and metro; tram and streetcar; rail and train); empty for a type LOOM has no name for. A numeric mode keeps its own code.

StopCounts.description: Rows of stops.txt by location_type, and the total.

Inspection.description: A feed as the Inspect screen shows it.

tables.description: The GTFS tables present, by stem.

frequency_trips.description: Trips with frequencies.txt windows: templates, expanded into runs when the day is built.

service.description: The window and the engine's day from the anchor, as feeds.service answers them; null when the feed has no calendar, with a warning saying so.

suggested_mode.description: A LOOM mode from the route types: all for a feed with nothing but rail-like types, else the most common rail-like type, else the most common. The app shows it; the person decides.

warnings.description: Sentences for a person: a headway-based timetable, an expired or unstarted calendar, a calendar_dates-only schedule, routes without short names, several operators in one feed.

StageName.description: One of the pipeline's four stages, in order.

RenderStageParams.description: One stored stage graph of a layout, drawn as SVG, with its counts (E15): what a geographic view shows beside the schematic map. Never lays out; a stage that is not stored is refused with kind layout.

width.description: The drawing's width in CSS pixels; the canvas grows for labels.

svg.description: A self-contained SVG document, themed through CSS variables with literal fallbacks.

ErrorData.description: The `data` of an error response. `hint` is a sentence for a person and is what a UI shows; `detail` says where, for a log.
